statement.text:
(G. M. Bergman). The width of a group G with respect to a generating set X
means the supremum over all g ∈ G of the least length of a group word in elements
of X expressing g. A group G has finite width if the width of G with respect to every
generating set is finite. Does there exist a countably infinite group of finite width?
   All known infinite groups of finite width (infinite permutation groups, infinite-
dimensional general linear groups, and some other groups) are uncountable
(G. M. Bergman, Bull. London Math. Soc., 38 (2006), 429–440, and references
therein).                                                                    V. Tolstykh
